To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) consumers from different countries have different brand concepts, which can be represented as different abstract concepts; (2) the abstract concepts are differentially associated with the four brand value dimensions; (3) the abstract concepts and brand value dimensions can be represented as points in a multidimensional space; (4) the four brand value dimension are related to each other in different ways across countries; (5) the four brand concepts are related to each others in different ways across the four countries; and

(a) the abstract meanings associated with brand concepts differ across countries and (b) the abstract meanings of the same brand concept are more congruent with the values of consumers in the country where the brand originated than with the values of foreign consumers.

the brand value dimensions uncovered by the pilot study are consistent with the dimensions of human values, and that the brand concepts representing the brand values are more effective in enhancing brand attitudes when the concepts are culturally congruent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how consumers perceive brands and how they make sense of brand concepts.
the role of values in the formation of brand meaning and brand attitudes.
the question of whether the abstract meanings that consumers associate with brands are consistent with the abstract meanings that are intended by the marketers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brand concepts are not only representations of brand values, but also representations of human values, which are in line with the results of previous studies (e.g., Rucker & Galinsky, 2008).

the self-enhancement value dimension is most strongly associated with the brand concepts of self-enhancement and openness, and the individualism value dimension is most closely associated with the brand concept of openness.

the results from Study 1 and Study 2 provide evidence of the existence of the four high level brand value dimensions, which are self-enhancement, openness, security, and benevolence, across the United States, China, Canada, and Turkey, and that these four high level brand values are related to brand concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to understand the role of human values in the process of advertising effectiveness, and we are trying to do it by looking at the relationship between values and advertising concepts.
the self-enhancement value dimension is a universal construct that is highly related with individualism, and the openness value dimension is highly related with collectivism.
we are not only able to identify the brand concepts that are most effective at communicating brand values but we are also able to determine which brand concepts work best in which countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
brand concepts are not just a convenient means of organizing the brand meanings that are activated by a brand.
brands that are congruent with the values of the target culture are more favorably evaluated by the target consumers than those that are not congruent.
brands can communicate a variety of meanings to consumers, and that the meanings that brands convey to consumers depend on the cultural context.
